newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU gas oil stocks seen high again in January.
newsitem.headline: EU gas oil stocks seen high again in January.

text.p: European Union figures to be released on Tuesday are expected to show high gas oil stocks in January, confirming that the spotlight on the distillate market is fading, analysts said.
"Year on year, the increase (for January) is likely to be around three percent," said Cindy Poynter of oil consultants Bonner and Moore.
Despite a very cold first two weeks of the year, analysts say many gas oil buyers had already made their essential purchases.
"A lot of gas oil seems to be held by refiners. We don't expect much of a draw," said Leslie Owens of oil consultants Petroleum Economics.
Some analysts even suspect that gas oil stocks actually grew in January as ice froze many waterways in the first two weeks and refiners found no buyers during the subsequent thaw.

"Historically, there's usually a small distillate draw, but I feel there may have been a small build because if you speak to refiners there seems to be a lot of material left," said Geoff Pyne, energy economist at Swiss bank UBS.
Gasoline is expected to appear healthier with stocks below year-ago levels, despite a likely seasonal build.
"Gasoline is about a million tonnes below historical levels. We would see stocks being about four percent below end of January 1996 levels," said Poynter.
However, refiners keen to find a dominant product to lift slack margins should not be lulled into optimism by gasoline.
"There's still oversupply. There's still an overhang," said Poynter.
The only prospects for shortage is likely to be crude oil.
"We ought to be looking at crude. It is the only thing that is tight. Refinery runs have been high and I would guess there was a small draw," said Pyne of UBS.
He added that Europe required another 15/16 million barrels to return to historical normality.
"That'll take more than a couple of months," he said.
